claim: Malaria caused an estimated 249 million new cases and more than 608,000 deaths in 2022.
source: Despite global efforts to combat malaria, the disease caused an estimated 249 million new cases and more than 608,000 deaths in 2022 (World Malaria Report 2023).
evidence: Supported by citation to World Malaria Report 2023

claim: Plasmodium falciparum is the most lethal of the six known Plasmodium species that can infect humans.
source: Among the six known Plasmodium species that can infect humans, Plasmodium falciparum is the most lethal, causing the majority of annual deaths (Cowman et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Cowman et al., 2012

claim: The intraerythrocytic developmental cycle (IDC) of P. falciparum is responsible for the clinical symptoms of malaria.
source: The intraerythrocytic developmental cycle (IDC) of P. falciparum is responsible for the clinical symptoms of malaria.
evidence: Supported by established scientific knowledge about malaria pathogenesis

claim: Merozoites generated during the liver stage enter the circulatory system and invade red blood cells (RBCs).
source: The IDC commences when merozoites generated during the liver stage enter the circulatory system and invade red blood cells (RBCs).
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of Plasmodium life cycle

claim: Parasites undergo multiple developmental phases with distinct morphological characteristics (ring, trophozoite, and schizont) while growing inside RBCs.
source: While growing inside RBCs, parasites undergo multiple developmental phases with distinct morphological characteristics (ring, trophozoite, and schizont).
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of Plasmodium developmental stages

claim: Maturation and schizogony lead to the formation of 16–32 daughter merozoites destined to invade new RBCs.
source: Maturation and schizogony lead to the formation of 16–32 daughter merozoites destined to invade new RBCs (Singh et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singh et al., 2010

claim: A small fraction (<10%) of parasites differentiate into non-replicative sexual gametocytes.
source: A small fraction (<10%) of parasites differentiate into non-replicative sexual gametocytes, which are transmitted to the mosquito during a second blood meal to complete sexual development.
evidence: Supported by established knowledge of Plasmodium sexual differentiation

claim: Approximately 90% of genes across the P. falciparum genome are transcribed during the asexual blood stage in a cascade of gene expression.
source: Approximately 90% of genes across the P. falciparum genome are transcribed during the asexual blood stage in a cascade of gene expression believed to be controlled by both sequence-specific transcription factors and dynamic epigenetic changes to chromatin (Painter et al., 2011; Toenhake et al., 2018; Jeninga et al., 2019; Hollin et al., 2021).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: The gene regulatory toolbox in malaria parasites is lacking many transcriptional regulatory factors conserved in other eukaryotes.
source: The gene regulatory toolbox in malaria parasites is lacking many transcriptional regulatory factors conserved in other eukaryotes (Gardner et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citation to Gardner et al., 2002

claim: There are 28 putative APETALA2 (ApiAP2) TFs identified in P. falciparum.
source: There are 28 putative APETALA2 (ApiAP2) TFs identified in P. falciparum, each protein containing 1–3 AP2 DNA binding domains (Painter et al., 2011; Jeninga et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Painter et al., 2011 and Jeninga et al., 2019

claim: Each ApiAP2 protein contains 1–3 AP2 DNA binding domains.
source: There are 28 putative APETALA2 (ApiAP2) TFs identified in P. falciparum, each protein containing 1–3 AP2 DNA binding domains (Painter et al., 2011; Jeninga et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Painter et al., 2011 and Jeninga et al., 2019

claim: Over 70% of ApiAP2 proteins are expressed in the asexual blood stage of the lifecycle.
source: ApiAP2 proteins in Plasmodium species display a wide array of functions during parasite development in both the vertebrate host and the mosquito vector, but surprisingly, over 70% of ApiAP2 proteins are expressed in the asexual blood stage of the lifecycle (Bozdech et al., 2003; Le Roch et al., 2003; Chappell et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bozdech et al., 2003; Le Roch et al., 2003; Chappell et al., 2020

claim: PfMORC (PF3D7_1468100) interacts with a suite of nuclear proteins, including APETALA2 (ApiAP2) transcription factors.
source: We show that PfMORC (PF3D7_1468100) interacts with a suite of nuclear proteins, including APETALA2 (ApiAP2) transcription factors (PfAP2-G5, PfAP2-O5, PfAP2-I, PF3D7_0420300, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_1107800, and PF3D7_1239200), a DNA helicase DS60 (PF3D7_1227100), and other chromatin remodelers (PfCHD1 and PfEELM2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry analysis presented in the manuscript

claim: PfMORC interacts with DNA helicase DS60 (PF3D7_1227100).
source: We show that PfMORC (PF3D7_1468100) interacts with a suite of nuclear proteins, including APETALA2 (ApiAP2) transcription factors (PfAP2-G5, PfAP2-O5, PfAP2-I, PF3D7_0420300, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_1107800, and PF3D7_1239200), a DNA helicase DS60 (PF3D7_1227100), and other chromatin remodelers (PfCHD1 and PfEELM2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry analysis

claim: PfMORC interacts with chromatin remodelers PfCHD1 and PfEELM2.
source: We show that PfMORC (PF3D7_1468100) interacts with a suite of nuclear proteins, including APETALA2 (ApiAP2) transcription factors (PfAP2-G5, PfAP2-O5, PfAP2-I, PF3D7_0420300, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_1107800, and PF3D7_1239200), a DNA helicase DS60 (PF3D7_1227100), and other chromatin remodelers (PfCHD1 and PfEELM2).
evidence: Supported by experimental data from co-immunoprecipitation and mass spectrometry analysis

claim: Transcriptomic analysis of PfMORCHA-glmS knockdown parasites revealed 163 differentially expressed genes belonging to hypervariable multigene families.
source: Transcriptomic analysis of PfMORCHA-glmS knockdown parasites revealed 163 differentially expressed genes belonging to hypervariable multigene families, along with upregulation of genes mostly involved in host cell invasion.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript

claim: PfMORC knockdown leads to upregulation of genes mostly involved in host cell invasion.
source: Transcriptomic analysis of PfMORCHA-glmS knockdown parasites revealed 163 differentially expressed genes belonging to hypervariable multigene families, along with upregulation of genes mostly involved in host cell invasion.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and GO analysis presented in the manuscript

claim: PfMORC is recruited to repressed, multigene families, including the var genes in subtelomeric chromosomal regions.
source: In vivo genome-wide chromatin occupancy analysis during both trophozoite and schizont stages of development demonstrates that PfMORC is recruited to repressed, multigene families, including the var genes in subtelomeric chromosomal regions.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data presented in the manuscript

claim: PfMORC is found in chromatin complexes that play a role in the epigenetic control of asexual blood stage transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization.
source: Collectively, we find that PfMORC is found in chromatin complexes that play a role in the epigenetic control of asexual blood stage transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization.
evidence: Supported by integration of proteomic, ChIP-seq, and RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript

claim: A quantitative mass spectrometry-based analysis of the parasite protein interaction network has revealed links between ApiAP2 TFs and many chromatin remodelers.
source: A quantitative mass spectrometry-based analysis of the parasite protein interaction network has revealed links between ApiAP2 TFs and many chromatin remodelers, such as an extended Egl-27 and MTA1 homology 2 (EELM2) domain-containing proteins (PF3D7_0519800 and PF3D7_1141800), histone deacetylase protein 1 (HDAC1; PF3D7_0925700), and the microrchidia family protein PfMORC (PF3D7_1468100) (Hillier et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Hillier et al., 2019

claim: Genome-wide mutagenesis studies revealed that pfmorc is essential for parasite proliferation.
source: Genome-wide mutagenesis studies revealed that several genes within these proposed networks, including pfmorc, are essential for parasite proliferation (Bushell et al., 2017; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bushell et al., 2017 and Zhang et al., 2018

claim: PfMORC was unable to be deleted using a targeted deletion strategy, suggesting it is essential for parasite growth.
source: Using a targeted deletion strategy, we previously were unable to delete pfmorc, further suggesting that it is essential for parasite growth (Singh et al., 2021a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singh et al., 2021a

claim: PfMORC was identified in a chromatin complex containing the chromatin remodeling protein PfISWI (PF3D7_0624600) located at var gene promoter regions.
source: Previous work identified PfMORC in a chromatin complex containing the chromatin remodeling protein PfISWI (PF3D7_0624600) located at var gene promoter regions (Bryant et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Bryant et al., 2020

claim: All P. falciparum strains encode roughly 60 highly polymorphic var genes.
source: All P. falciparum strains encode roughly 60 highly polymorphic var genes, but through an epigenetic allelic exclusion mechanism, each parasite is thought to expresses a single allele (Real et al., 2022; Schneider et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Real et al., 2022 and Schneider et al., 2023

claim: Each parasite expresses a single var allele through an epigenetic allelic exclusion mechanism.
source: All P. falciparum strains encode roughly 60 highly polymorphic var genes, but through an epigenetic allelic exclusion mechanism, each parasite is thought to expresses a single allele (Real et al., 2022; Schneider et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Real et al., 2022 and Schneider et al., 2023

claim: TgMORC functions as a repressor of sex-associated genes by recruiting the TgHDAC3 histone deacetylase in Toxoplasma gondii.
source: In the related apicomplexan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, TgMORC functions as a repressor of sex-associated genes by recruiting the TgHDAC3 histone deacetylase and forming heterogenous complexes with 11 ApiAP2 TFs (Farhat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Farhat et al., 2020

claim: TgMORC forms heterogenous complexes with 11 ApiAP2 TFs in Toxoplasma gondii.
source: In the related apicomplexan parasite Toxoplasma gondii, TgMORC functions as a repressor of sex-associated genes by recruiting the TgHDAC3 histone deacetylase and forming heterogenous complexes with 11 ApiAP2 TFs (Farhat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Farhat et al., 2020

claim: MORC proteins canonically consist of a catalytic ATPase domain at the N-terminus and a C-terminal protein-protein interaction domain containing one or more coiled-coils.
source: MORC proteins canonically consist of two major conserved regions: (1) a catalytic ATPase domain at the N-terminus (comprising a GHKL [Gyrase, HSP90, Histidine kinase, and MutL] domain and S5 fold domain) and (2) a C-terminal protein-protein interaction domain containing one or more coiled-coils (Koch et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to Koch et al., 2017

claim: The conserved MORC gene family is present in most eukaryotes (with the exception of fungi).
source: The conserved MORC gene family is present in most eukaryotes (with the exception of fungi), often with multiple paralogs per genome (Dong et al., 2018), and has been extensively investigated in various model systems in the context of epigenetic gene regulation.
evidence: Supported by citation to Dong et al., 2018

claim: In plants, MORC proteins function in gene repression and heterochromatin compaction.
source: In plants, MORC proteins function in gene repression and heterochromatin compaction (Koch et al., 2017; Zhong et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Koch et al., 2017 and Zhong et al., 2023

claim: Most metazoans possess 5–7 MORC paralogs.
source: While most metazoans possess 5–7 MORC paralogs, apicomplexan parasites contain a single morc gene (Iyer et al., 2008a), which encodes not only the canonical animal-like GHKL ATPase domain, but also three Kelch-repeats, and a CW-type zinc-finger domain not found in mammalian MORCs (Farhat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Iyer et al., 2008a

claim: Apicomplexan parasites contain a single morc gene.
source: While most metazoans possess 5–7 MORC paralogs, apicomplexan parasites contain a single morc gene (Iyer et al., 2008a), which encodes not only the canonical animal-like GHKL ATPase domain, but also three Kelch-repeats, and a CW-type zinc-finger domain not found in mammalian MORCs (Farhat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Iyer et al., 2008a

claim: Apicomplexan MORC proteins encode three Kelch-repeats and a CW-type zinc-finger domain not found in mammalian MORCs.
source: While most metazoans possess 5–7 MORC paralogs, apicomplexan parasites contain a single morc gene (Iyer et al., 2008a), which encodes not only the canonical animal-like GHKL ATPase domain, but also three Kelch-repeats, and a CW-type zinc-finger domain not found in mammalian MORCs (Farhat et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to Farhat et al., 2020

claim: The unique domain architecture of apicomplexan MORC proteins suggests they may have parasite-specific roles.
source: This unique domain architecture suggests that the apicomplexan MORC proteins may have parasite-specific roles.
evidence: Inferred from the unique domain architecture described

claim: PfEELM2 (PF3D7_0519800) was the top enriched protein in PfMORC co-immunoprecipitation with 20.8-fold enrichment.
source: From these candidate PfMORC-interacting proteins, the top enriched protein (20.8-fold enrichment) was PfEELM2 (PF3D7_0519800, -log10 p-value 3.43).
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data from co-immunoprecipitation experiments

claim: PfEELM2 was previously predicted as a PfMORC interactor.
source: PfEELM2 was previously predicted as a PfMORC interactor (Hillier et al., 2019) and identified in a quantitative histone peptide pulldown to be consistently recruited to H2B.Z_K13/14/18a (Hoeijmakers et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to Hillier et al., 2019 and Hoeijmakers et al., 2019

claim: PfAP2-G5 (PF3D7_1139300) was enriched 20.5-fold in PfMORC co-immunoprecipitation.
source: PfAP2-G5 (PF3D7_1139300, -log10 p-value 0.22) and PfAP2-O5 (PF3D7_1449500, -log10 p-value 0.41) were enriched 20.5-fold and 14.99-fold, respectively, suggesting that these factors are likely major components in complex with PfMORC.
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data from co-immunoprecipitation experiments

claim: PfAP2-O5 (PF3D7_1449500) was enriched 14.99-fold in PfMORC co-immunoprecipitation.
source: PfAP2-G5 (PF3D7_1139300, -log10 p-value 0.22) and PfAP2-O5 (PF3D7_1449500, -log10 p-value 0.41) were enriched 20.5-fold and 14.99-fold, respectively, suggesting that these factors are likely major components in complex with PfMORC.
evidence: Supported by mass spectrometry data from co-immunoprecipitation experiments

claim: PfAP2-G5 and PfAP2-O5 are likely major components in complex with PfMORC.
source: PfAP2-G5 (PF3D7_1139300, -log10 p-value 0.22) and PfAP2-O5 (PF3D7_1449500, -log10 p-value 0.41) were enriched 20.5-fold and 14.99-fold, respectively, suggesting that these factors are likely major components in complex with PfMORC.
evidence: Inferred from high fold enrichment in co-immunoprecipitation experiments

claim: PfMORC localizes to subtelomeric regions on all chromosomes across the P. falciparum genome.
source: We identified PfMORC localized to subtelomeric regions on all chromosomes across the P. falciparum genome, with additional occupancy at internal heterochromatic islands (Figure 2A and B).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2A and B

claim: PfMORC was bound upstream and within the gene bodies of many hypervariable multigene families.
source: Within the subtelomeric regions, PfMORC was bound upstream and within the gene bodies of many hypervariable multigene families (Figure 2C), including var genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 2), rif genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 3), and stevor genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 4).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2C and supplementary figures

claim: Predicted binding sites between the 30 hpi and 40 hpi timepoints showed a high degree of overlap.
source: Predicted binding sites (across both biological replicates) between the 30 hpi and 40 hpi timepoints showed a high degree of overlap, suggesting that PfMORC binds many of the same regions throughout the later stages of asexual development when PfMORC is highly expressed (Figure 2D).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2D

claim: PfMORC occupancy forms sharp peaks within, and adjacent to, HP1-bound regions.
source: As opposed to the binding of other proteins at the subtelomeric regions, such as the heterochromatin protein 1 (PfHP1) (Flueck et al., 2010), PfMORC occupancy is not widespread. Instead, it forms sharp peaks within, and adjacent to, HP1-bound regions (Figure 2F), suggesting a unique role for PfMORC in heterochromatin condensation, boundary demarcation, and gene repression.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 2F

claim: PfMORC has a unique role in heterochromatin condensation, boundary demarcation, and gene repression.
source: As opposed to the binding of other proteins at the subtelomeric regions, such as the heterochromatin protein 1 (PfHP1) (Flueck et al., 2010), PfMORC occupancy is not widespread. Instead, it forms sharp peaks within, and adjacent to, HP1-bound regions (Figure 2F), suggesting a unique role for PfMORC in heterochromatin condensation, boundary demarcation, and gene repression.
evidence: Inferred from the distinct binding pattern of PfMORC compared to HP1

claim: 149 putative gene targets were identified at 30 hpi and 102 gene targets at 40 hpi.
source: This resulted in 149 putative gene targets at 30 hpi and 102 gene targets at 40 hpi.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: 84 overlapping genes between 30 hpi and 40 hpi timepoints include many var genes, rRNA genes, and genes encoding exported proteins.
source: A close examination of the 84 overlapping genes shows that many are var genes, rRNA genes, and genes encoding exported proteins (Supplementary file 4), with GO terms related to cell adhesion, host‒pathogen interactions, and antigenic variation (Supplementary file 5).
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data analysis and GO term enrichment

claim: There is a degree of overlap between the binding sites of six ApiAP2 TFs and PfMORC.
source: Interestingly, there is a degree of overlap between the binding sites of all six ApiAP2 TFs and PfMORC, suggesting that PfMORC and these ApiAP2 TFs may cooperate in the regulation of gene expression at these loci (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by comparison of ChIP-seq datasets shown in Figure 3A and B

claim: PfMORC and ApiAP2 TFs may cooperate in the regulation of gene expression at overlapping loci.
source: Interestingly, there is a degree of overlap between the binding sites of all six ApiAP2 TFs and PfMORC, suggesting that PfMORC and these ApiAP2 TFs may cooperate in the regulation of gene expression at these loci (Figure 3A and B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Inferred from overlapping binding sites in ChIP-seq data

claim: DNA motif enrichment analysis identified RGTGCAW or TGCACACA as common motifs at PfMORC binding sites.
source: The common motifs identified across replicates and timepoints are RGTGCAW or TGCACACA, both of which are similar or identical to the in vitro and/or in vivo DNA-binding motif of PfAP2-I (RGTGCAW) or PF3D7_0420300 (TGCACACA), respectively, suggesting that these ApiAP2 factors may play major roles in PfMORC recruitment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Supported by DNA motif enrichment analysis shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2

claim: PfAP2-I or PF3D7_0420300 may play major roles in PfMORC recruitment.
source: The common motifs identified across replicates and timepoints are RGTGCAW or TGCACACA, both of which are similar or identical to the in vitro and/or in vivo DNA-binding motif of PfAP2-I (RGTGCAW) or PF3D7_0420300 (TGCACACA), respectively, suggesting that these ApiAP2 factors may play major roles in PfMORC recruitment (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Inferred from motif similarity to ApiAP2 binding sites

claim: PfMORC co-localizes with the depletion of H3K36me2 at both 30 hpi and 40 hpi.
source: In addition to overlapping occupancy with ApiAP2 TFs, we found that PfMORC co-localizes with the depletion of H3K36me2 (Figure 3C and D), which is demarcated by the SET2 methyltransferase (Jiang et al., 2013), both at 30 hpi and 40h pi.
evidence: Supported by comparison of ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3C and D

claim: No significant co-localization was found between PfMORC and other epigenetic marks (H2A.Z, H3K9ac, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K18ac, H3K9me3, H3K36me2/3, H4K20me3, and H3K4me1).
source: No other significant co-localization was found between PfMORC and other epigenetic marks (H2A.Z, H3K9ac, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K18ac, H3K9me3, H3K36me2/3, H4K20me3, and H3K4me1) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), suggesting it has a unique binding preference not shared with other heterochromatin markers.
evidence: Supported by comparison of ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3

claim: PfMORC has a unique binding preference not shared with other heterochromatin markers.
source: No other significant co-localization was found between PfMORC and other epigenetic marks (H2A.Z, H3K9ac, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K18ac, H3K9me3, H3K36me2/3, H4K20me3, and H3K4me1) (Figure 3—figure supplement 3), suggesting it has a unique binding preference not shared with other heterochromatin markers.
evidence: Inferred from lack of co-localization with other epigenetic marks

claim: Treatment with 2.5 mM GlcN results in a 50% knockdown of PfMORC protein but does not cause any growth delay.
source: We previously demonstrated that treatment with 2.5 mM GlcN results in a 50% knockdown of PfMORC protein but does not cause any growth delay; using >2.5 mM GlcN caused a measurable slow growth and reduced parasitemia (Singh et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singh et al., 2021b

claim: Using >2.5 mM GlcN caused a measurable slow growth and reduced parasitemia.
source: We previously demonstrated that treatment with 2.5 mM GlcN results in a 50% knockdown of PfMORC protein but does not cause any growth delay; using >2.5 mM GlcN caused a measurable slow growth and reduced parasitemia (Singh et al., 2021b).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singh et al., 2021b

claim: PfMORC knockdown resulted in 60 genes with more abundant transcripts and 103 genes with reduced transcripts.
source: Among these, 60 genes display more abundant transcripts, whereas 103 genes were reduced relative to control parasites grown without GlcN (Figure 4A).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4A

claim: Upregulated genes in PfMORC knockdown include several rhoptry-associated genes, notably PfRON2 (PF3D7_1452000) and PfRON3 (PF3D7_1252100).
source: More specifically, upregulated genes implicated in the invasion of merozoites were found to be expressed prematurely upon PfMORC KD; these include several rhoptry-associated genes, notably PfRON2 (PF3D7_1452000) and PfRON3 (PF3D7_1252100).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis

claim: PfRON2 and PfRON3 are part of a micronemal complex at the erythrocyte membrane where PfRON2 anchors PfAMA1 to facilitate merozoite invasion.
source: Both PfRON2 and PfRON3 are part of a micronemal complex at the erythrocyte membrane where PfRON2 anchors PfAMA1 to facilitate merozoite invasion (Srinivasan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Srinivasan et al., 2013

claim: PfSUB3 (PF3D7_0507200), PfSERA5 (PF3D7_0207600), and PfDPAP3 (PF3D7_0404700) are critical for schizont rupture.
source: In addition, PfSUB3 (PF3D7_0507200), PfSERA5 (PF3D7_0207600), and PfDPAP3 (PF3D7_0404700), all of which are critical for schizont rupture (Yeoh et al., 2007; Arastu-Kapur et al., 2008), were among the upregulated DEGs (Figure 4C).
evidence: Supported by citations to Yeoh et al., 2007 and Arastu-Kapur et al., 2008

claim: Depletion of PfMORC leads to the upregulation of invasion-related genes.
source: In general, we found that depletion of PfMORC leads to the upregulation of invasion-related genes, which suggests that PfMORC has an additional function in the regulation of genes specifically associated with RBC invasion.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and GO analysis

claim: PfMORC has an additional function in the regulation of genes specifically associated with RBC invasion.
source: In general, we found that depletion of PfMORC leads to the upregulation of invasion-related genes, which suggests that PfMORC has an additional function in the regulation of genes specifically associated with RBC invasion.
evidence: Inferred from upregulation of invasion-related genes upon PfMORC knockdown

claim: Many downregulated genes in PfMORC knockdown belong to the clonally variant var multigene family.
source: Many of the genes enriched in the downregulated group belong to the clonally variant var multigene family that represents 60 members encoding the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins (PfEMP1), which upon switching expression aid in pathogenesis and immune evasion (Guizetti and Scherf, 2013).
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data analysis and citation to Guizetti and Scherf, 2013

claim: The var multigene family represents 60 members encoding the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins (PfEMP1).
source: Many of the genes enriched in the downregulated group belong to the clonally variant var multigene family that represents 60 members encoding the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins (PfEMP1), which upon switching expression aid in pathogenesis and immune evasion (Guizetti and Scherf, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Guizetti and Scherf, 2013

claim: PfEMP1 switching expression aids in pathogenesis and immune evasion.
source: Many of the genes enriched in the downregulated group belong to the clonally variant var multigene family that represents 60 members encoding the P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane proteins (PfEMP1), which upon switching expression aid in pathogenesis and immune evasion (Guizetti and Scherf, 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Guizetti and Scherf, 2013

claim: The low correlation between ChIP-seq gene targets and RNA-seq DEGs suggests that PfMORC genome-wide occupancy is more likely involved in chromatin structure, rather than specific regulation of gene targets.
source: The low correlation between the ChIP-seq gene targets and the RNA-seq DEGs suggests that PfMORC genome-wide occupancy is more likely involved in chromatin structure, rather than specific regulation of gene targets (Figure 4E).
evidence: Inferred from comparison of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data shown in Figure 4E

claim: PfMORC localizes to sites to aid in chromatin condensation, as shown in other eukaryotic systems.
source: Likely, PfMORC localizes to these sites to aid in chromatin condensation, as shown in other eukaryotic systems (Zhang et al., 2019; Zhong et al., 2023).
evidence: Supported by citations to Zhang et al., 2019 and Zhong et al., 2023

claim: Periodic gene expression during the asexual blood stage directly corresponds to the timing in which gene products are needed.
source: Periodic gene expression during the asexual blood stage directly corresponds to the timing in which gene products are needed (Bozdech et al., 2003) and shows oscillation patterns associated with circadian rhythms (Smith et al., 2020; Subudhi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Bozdech et al., 2003; Smith et al., 2020; Subudhi et al., 2020

claim: Gene expression shows oscillation patterns associated with circadian rhythms during the asexual blood stage.
source: Periodic gene expression during the asexual blood stage directly corresponds to the timing in which gene products are needed (Bozdech et al., 2003) and shows oscillation patterns associated with circadian rhythms (Smith et al., 2020; Subudhi et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citations to Smith et al., 2020 and Subudhi et al., 2020

claim: ApiAP2 proteins have been reported in transcriptional silencing of clonally variant genes, regulation of invasion genes, and sexual commitment.
source: To date, ApiAP2 proteins have been reported in transcriptional silencing of clonally variant genes, regulation of invasion genes, and sexual commitment, acting through interaction with other epigenetic factors, such as heterochromatin protein 1 [PfHP1 (Flueck et al., 2010; Brancucci et al., 2014; Fraschka et al., 2018)], bromodomain protein 1 [PfBDP1 (Santos et al., 2017; Josling et al., 2020; Quinn et al., 2022)], or general control non-depressible 5 [PfGCN5 (Miao et al., 2021)].
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to published research

claim: TgMORC was identified in a complex with HDAC1, AP2XII-2, and AP2XII-1:AP2XI-2 in Toxoplasma gondii.
source: Recently, the T. gondii ortholog TgMORC was identified in a complex with HDAC1, AP2XII-2, and AP2XII-1:AP2XI-2and orchestrates epigenetic rewiring of sexual gene transcription (Farhat et al., 2020; Srivastava et al., 2023; Antunes et al., 2024).
evidence: Supported by citations to Farhat et al., 2020; Srivastava et al., 2023; Antunes et al., 2024

claim: PfMORC was associated with PfAP2-G5, which is essential for gametocytogenesis.
source: More specifically, PfMORC was associated with PfAP2-G5, which is essential for gametocytogenesis (Shang et al., 2021b), PfAP2-I, which is required for the expression of many invasion-related genes (Santos et al., 2017), and with other ApiAP2 TFs of unknown function (PfAP2-O5, PF3D7_1107800, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_0420300, and PF3D7_1239200).
evidence: Supported by co-immunoprecipitation data and citation to Shang et al., 2021b

claim: PfAP2-I is required for the expression of many invasion-related genes.
source: More specifically, PfMORC was associated with PfAP2-G5, which is essential for gametocytogenesis (Shang et al., 2021b), PfAP2-I, which is required for the expression of many invasion-related genes (Santos et al., 2017), and with other ApiAP2 TFs of unknown function (PfAP2-O5, PF3D7_1107800, PF3D7_0613800, PF3D7_0420300, and PF3D7_1239200).
evidence: Supported by citation to Santos et al., 2017

claim: The identification of PfISW1 and PfCHD1 in association with PfMORC strengthens the link between PfMORC and chromatin remodeling.
source: The identification of PfISW1 and PfCHD1 in association with PfMORC strengthens the link between PfMORC and chromatin remodeling.
evidence: Inferred from co-immunoprecipitation data identifying these chromatin remodelers

claim: PfMORC may participate in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression during the IDC, notably the specific regulation of var genes.
source: This finding suggests that PfMORC may participate in regulating chromatin structure and gene expression during the IDC, notably the specific regulation of var genes.
evidence: Inferred from association with chromatin remodelers and localization to var genes

claim: In Arabidopsis, AtMORC paralogs are important in gene regulation by chromatin compaction.
source: Recent work in Arabidopsis has further confirmed the importance of AtMORC paralogs in gene regulation by chromatin compaction (Zhong et al., 2023), which resembles the function of PfMORC in P. falciparum.
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2023

claim: In T. gondii, the major function of TgMORC was in the repression of sex determination genes.
source: Interestingly, in T. gondii, the major function of TgMORC was in the repression of sex determination genes (Farhat et al., 2020), suggesting MORC family proteins have the capacity to perform diverse functions across eukaryotic organisms.
evidence: Supported by citation to Farhat et al., 2020

claim: PfHP1 has been shown to regulate sexual commitment by repressing PfAP2-G and virulence genes expression.
source: The role of PfHP1 has been shown in regulating sexual commitment by repressing PfAP2-G and virulence genes expression (Brancucci et al., 2014), whereas gametocyte development 1 (PfGDV1) displaces PfHP1 itself and induces asexual developing parasites to sexual differentiation (Filarsky et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citations to Brancucci et al., 2014 and Filarsky et al., 2018

claim: PfGDV1 displaces PfHP1 and induces asexual developing parasites to sexual differentiation.
source: The role of PfHP1 has been shown in regulating sexual commitment by repressing PfAP2-G and virulence genes expression (Brancucci et al., 2014), whereas gametocyte development 1 (PfGDV1) displaces PfHP1 itself and induces asexual developing parasites to sexual differentiation (Filarsky et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Filarsky et al., 2018

claim: AtMORC-mediated regulation of transcription may be due to both direct chromatin interactions and indirect association via sequence-specific transcription factors.
source: In addition, a recent study in Arabidopsis reported that AtMORC-mediated regulation of transcription may be due to both direct chromatin interactions and indirect association via sequence-specific transcription factors (Zhong et al., 2023) consistent with a complex landscape of chromatin remodeling by MORC proteins.
evidence: Supported by citation to Zhong et al., 2023

claim: H3K36me2 has been shown to act as a global repressive effector in P. falciparum.
source: We also interrogated the co-localization of PfMORC and numerous epigenetic profiles (H2A.Z, H3K9ac, H3K4me3, H3K27ac, H3K18ac, H3K9me3, H3K36me2/3, H4K20me3, and H3K4me1), with a specific focus on H3K36me2, since this histone modification has been shown to act as a global repressive effector in P. falciparum (Karmodiya et al., 2015) and other organisms (Strahl et al., 2002; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Karmodiya et al., 2015; Strahl et al., 2002; Wagner and Carpenter, 2012

claim: The upregulated DEGs in PfMORC knockdown were enriched with genes related to invasion.
source: Therefore, we investigated the DEGs in PfMORC knockdown parasites and found two distinct subsets of enriched genes. The upregulated DEGs were enriched with genes related to invasion, while the downregulated DEGs belong to hypervariable genes associated with parasite virulence.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and GO analysis

claim: The downregulated DEGs in PfMORC knockdown belong to hypervariable genes associated with parasite virulence.
source: Therefore, we investigated the DEGs in PfMORC knockdown parasites and found two distinct subsets of enriched genes. The upregulated DEGs were enriched with genes related to invasion, while the downregulated DEGs belong to hypervariable genes associated with parasite virulence.
evidence: Supported by RNA-seq data and GO analysis

claim: Expression of clonally variant genes occurs in a different but tightly regulated manner in IDC.
source: Overall, our data with PfMORC-KD revealed a change in the expression of both antigenically variable and invasion-related genes. Expression of clonally variant genes occurs in a different but tightly regulated manner in IDC (Scherf et al., 1998; Scherf et al., 2008), which, in the light of our data, may be regulated by PfMORC occupancy.
evidence: Supported by citations to Scherf et al., 1998 and Scherf et al., 2008

claim: Expression of clonally variant genes may be regulated by PfMORC occupancy.
source: Overall, our data with PfMORC-KD revealed a change in the expression of both antigenically variable and invasion-related genes. Expression of clonally variant genes occurs in a different but tightly regulated manner in IDC (Scherf et al., 1998; Scherf et al., 2008), which, in the light of our data, may be regulated by PfMORC occupancy.
evidence: Inferred from changes in clonally variant gene expression upon PfMORC knockdown

claim: Parasites in which PfMORC is knocked down display reduced sensitivity to melatonin.
source: We previously showed that parasites in which PfMORC is knocked down display reduced sensitivity to melatonin (Singh et al., 2021a).
evidence: Supported by citation to Singh et al., 2021a

claim: Melatonin does not exert its effect on gene expression through PfMORC, or PfMORC plays a minor role in the process.
source: We detected only very slight changes (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), suggesting that melatonin does not exert its effect on gene expression through PfMORC, or at least that the latter protein plays a minor role in the process.
evidence: Inferred from minimal changes in gene expression with melatonin treatment shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1

claim: PfMORC is localized at sub-telomeric regions and contains significant overlap with the binding sites of several ApiAP2 transcription factors.
source: Furthermore, we found that PfMORC is localized at sub-telomeric regions and contains significant overlap with the binding sites of several ApiAP2 transcription factors.
evidence: Supported by ChIP-seq data analysis

claim: PfMORC plays a role in the regulation of hypervariable genes that are essential for Plasmodium virulence and rhoptry genes critical to RBC invasion.
source: Our results support a role for PfMORC in the regulation of hypervariable genes that are essential for Plasmodium virulence and rhoptry genes critical to RBC invasion.
evidence: Supported by integration of ChIP-seq and RNA-seq data

claim: PfMORC plays an important role in chromatin organization and in the epigenetic regulation of gene expression through regulatory complexes with an array of transcription factors.
source: Collectively, our data identify an important role for PfMORC in chromatin organization, as well as in the epigenetic regulation of gene expression through regulatory complexes with an array of transcription factors, making it an attractive drug target.
evidence: Supported by integration of proteomic, ChIP-seq, and RNA-seq data

claim: PfMORC is an attractive drug target.
